messages.author: a08a2def4527ebe2
messages.subject: n_divergent, treedepth and thinning
parts:
Hi all, 

First, thank you for a very useful program! 

I have a simple question about thinning chains in Stan. I'm using CmdStan, but I think this applies to other interfaces too. 

Suppose I thin my chains, and there sometimes is a n_divergent error. Will I be able to see this from the output - or will I only see it if the n_divergent occurs in the iterations that have not been thinned?

Alternatively, is there a way of summing up the n_divergent along the way?

-op

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] n_divergent, treedepth and thinning
parts:
The latter — “thinning” is just a pruning of the Markov chain output.
Because the thinned states are not stored anywhere there is no way
to recover diagnostics such as the divergences.  That said, thinning
shouldn’t be necessary in Stan — if you have autocorrelations large
enough to necessitate thinning then you probably have substantial
problems with the model itself.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] n_divergent, treedepth and thinning
parts:
Thinning is always a bad idea in that it loses information.

And usually people set the number of effective samples higher
than they need for their inferential purposes.

Sometimes the information loss is necessary to get enough draws
to fit in memory or on disk. That's less of a problem in Stan
with lower autocorrelation time. It might still be necessary,
especially if you save all of a set of item-specific parameters.
For example, all the parameters for 1M students in an IRT model.
Then you're looking at around 10MB per iteration in a CSV file (about
ten bytes per real in ASCII), or 8GB for 1000 iterations.

- Bob
